enhanced_information: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is a procedure used to amplify DNA segments, not to separate clones from a genomic library. It requires the use of heat-resistant polymerases and is based on the activity of DNA polymerase, not RNA polymerase. PCR takes place in a controlled laboratory setting, not in the cellular cytoplasm. Evidence paths confirm the role of DNA polymerase in PCR and its amplification of DNA segments.
